title: bb_health freshness reasons: every category reachable, distinguishable, and reconciling with the headline

checks.name: an edited file is `hash-differs`
a deleted file is `file-gone`
an untouched file is `metadata-fast-path`
an unreadable file is `unreadable` (needs BOTH a mode change and a missed fast path)
checks.detail: f2 -> unreadable; chmod 000 alone yields metadata-fast-path because the stat still matches and the file is never opened

checks.name: and it is reported MISSING, never fresh
a same-content file with a changed mtime is `hash-match` — the bytes were actually read
checks.detail: f6 -> hash-match (touched mtime only, content identical; this is what separates the two 'fresh' verdicts)

checks.name: and it is reported FRESH, not stale
the two fresh kinds are genuinely different categories [negative]
an id with no index row is `no-row`
every category in the exported vocabulary is REACHABLE
reasons + unclassified == checked, exactly once
fresh == hash-match + metadata-fast-path
stale == hash-differs
missing == file-gone + unreadable + no-row
the two fresh splits are exposed, and they are the counts
every category key is present, even at zero
a complete scan is not marked as a sample
the edited and deleted counts are real
the default output carries the reason mix (not verbose-only)
checks.detail: freshness why: 8 fresh by mtime+size only (file not read — a same-size edit preserving the mtime reads as fresh); 1 stal

checks.name: it names the content change
checks.detail: freshness why: 8 fresh by mtime+size only (file not read — a same-size edit preserving the mtime reads as fresh); 1 stale: content changed (reindex these); 1 mi

checks.name: it names the deletion, with its different remedy
it states the fast path's error bound ON THE LINE
checks.detail: fresh by mtime+size only (file not read — a same-size edit preserving the mtime reads as fresh)

checks.name: and does not present a bare `N fresh` as if the bytes were read [negative]
checks.detail: the fast-path count must be attributed, not merged into 'fresh'

checks.name: the STALE_FILES warning names the mix
checks.detail: 1 stale and 1 missing of 10 indexed files (1 changed on disk, 1 deleted from disk)

checks.name: a SAMPLED breakdown says it is a sample
checks.detail: freshness why: 4 fresh by mtime+size only (file not read — a same-size edit preserving the mtime reads as fresh) — over the 4-file SAMPLE, not the pro

checks.name: and a complete one does not claim to be a sample
a reindexed index is genuinely clean
checks.detail: stale=0 missing=0 (deleting f1 back out of the index is the indexer's job, not this gate's)

checks.name: a clean index still renders a reason mix in prose, not category keys
checks.detail: freshness why: 9 fresh by mtime+size only (file not read — a same-size edit preserving the mtime reads as fresh)

checks.name: and the prose still attributes the fast path rather than saying 'fresh'

decisions.vocabulary: RowFreshnessReason is exported and typed at the resolver; a tally cannot be published without it
decisions.freshSplit: hash-match and metadata-fast-path are reported apart — one read the bytes, one did not
decisions.limitation: the metadata fast path's error bound is stated on the LINE, not only in a source comment
decisions.placement: the mix is in the DEFAULT output, not verbose: the defect is that the number is unactivable by default
decisions.reconciliation: reasons nest under status and must sum to `checked` exactly once

limitations: The unreadable case is produced with chmod, which does not restrict root — on a runner that ignores file modes the case degrades to a read that succeeds. The gate asserts the category is REACHABLE, not that it occurs on every platform.
